source.title: Implicit regularization in Heavy-ball momentum accelerated stochastic gradient descent
source.authors: Avrajit Ghosh; He Lyu; Xi-Tong Zhang; Rongrong Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how Heavy-ball momentum changes test accuracy in image classifiers, an optimizer setting related to the claim but outside its listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy, not the training-to-test error gap. The CIFAR tables compare SGD with momentum values at a matched effective learning rate; the MNIST comparison reports best test accuracy across learning rates or momentum values.
record.test_reason: The study tests Heavy-ball momentum versus plain gradient descent, which none of V1–V8 names. It does not compare adaptive optimizers, vary batch size, or measure magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps. Its discussion of flatness and batch noise does not test those versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that suitably configured momentum SGD outperforms plain SGD in almost all tested settings. They explain this through stronger implicit gradient regularization, while arguing that momentum's variance reduction can counteract the benefit. They also suggest that noise injection may amplify implicit gradient regularization.
record.recipe_differences: Studies Heavy-ball momentum versus plain SGD, rather than the listed random-label, width, architecture, adaptive-optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-measure, or memorized-example interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Momentum effects vary by dataset and architecture; the authors also report a smaller test-accuracy difference after learning-rate scheduling.

fits_no_version.finding: At effective learning rate 0.1 and batch size 640, β=0.8 gives higher mean test accuracy than β=0 for all eight CIFAR dataset–architecture combinations. Intermediate momentum values have exceptions; CIFAR-100 ResNet-50 peaks at β=0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heavy-ball momentum can improve image-classification test accuracy relative to plain SGD at matched effective learning rate, depending on architecture and momentum.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet-18 trained on 1,000 MNIST images, the selected best full-batch momentum test accuracy is 96.22%, versus 95.72% for GD. These maxima come from different hyperparameter sweeps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this experiment, the best reported full-batch momentum test accuracy exceeds the best reported GD test accuracy across the respective tested sweeps.

record.problems: The reported classification evidence emphasizes test accuracy and does not provide paired training accuracy or a measured training-test gap. CIFAR results average over three seeds and the last five epochs; uncertainty is substantial for some entries. MNIST best scores come from hyperparameter sweeps and are not matched training-error comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports scheduler experiments for ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 on CIFAR-10 in Appendix Section 5.2, but the supplied figures provide no numerical values; the text only says the momentum advantage persists slightly after scheduling. These are not separately rowed because values are figure-only and the statement is qualitative.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out performance under the same recipe, and chance-level random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD, and the effects of tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout versus no dropout and its dependence on configuration, dataset size, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T3 requires a result on a listed version; an adjacent optimizer experiment does not qualify. Test accuracy is an adequate held-out measure for several versions, so the decisive exclusion is the intervention mismatch, not the absence of a training–test gap. All CIFAR values and baselines match Table 1. Its uncertainty pools the last five epochs and three initializations, rather than reporting only between-seed uncertainty. The scheduler results are already declared in rows_left_out and bear on no listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, with held-out and training performance.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
